The Bachelor of Science in business analytics prepares students for careers that use data to support and inform business decision-making and management. They learn skills in a natural progression including assembling and managing data, displaying data, uncovering patterns in data, developing predictive models, and using these models to make better decisions across all business domains. Business analytics skills are in demand across a wide range of industries including healthcare, sports, marketing, finance, consulting, supply-chain operations, and information technology.

Students are encouraged to develop expertise in a functional business discipline such as supply-chain management, health care management, marketing or finance using elective coursework.

Program Objectives:

  • Gainful employment leveraging economic analytical skills in economics, policy, or in a related field.
  • Acceptance to a graduate degree program.

The general concentration provides an opportunity for a student to place particular emphasis on a specific business analytics or related field.

The Bachelor of Science in Computer Science program will help students develop the strong foundation in mathematics and computing they need to enter this high-demand, ever-evolving field. They will tap into their aptitude for problem-solving, hone their ability to think in the abstract, and develop the design skills to solve problems.

As a computer science major students will:

  • Develop the ability to analyze a problem, then identify and define the computing requirements appropriate to its solution,
  • Learn to design, implement, and evaluate a computer-based process, system, component, or program to meet specific needs,
  • Apply mathematical foundations, algorithmic principles, and computer science theory in the modeling and design of computer-based systems,
  • Become proficient in computer hardware, software, and theory, as defined by the Association of Computing Machinery (ACM) curriculum guidelines,
  • Learn to work effectively in a variety of contexts, using various languages, systems, and environments,
  • Begin to build leadership skills that will help them quickly advance their career,
  • Gain hands-on experience through an internship or co-op and an individual programming project,
  • Work with cutting-edge technology in state-of-the-art laboratories
  • Be prepared to enter one of the most in-demand career fields in the country,
  • Establish the skills they need to be a lifelong independent learner, a requirement for this evolving field.

The Master of Science in AI in Business and Analytics at the University of New Haven prepares students to help organizations turn large and complex datasets into actionable insights. Across industries, businesses need professionals who can collect, prepare and interpret data to support profitability, productivity, operational performance and decision-making.

The programme develops students’ knowledge of business practices, statistics and programming, with a focus on applying predictive analytics, machine learning and data visualization to business challenges. It was designed through collaboration among faculty in economics and business analytics, finance, marketing and management. Students can typically complete the degree in four semesters, or around 18 months.

The programme offers a specialised alternative to an MBA and equips graduates with a foundation for roles across a broad range of industries. These include established data-driven sectors such as e-commerce and finance, as well as fields increasingly adopting modern business practices, including healthcare, higher education, government and professional sports.

The Master of Science in Business Analytics program integrates knowledge of business domains with extensive knowledge of data management, machine learning, predictive analytics, and data visualization. The broad and intensive curriculum across a range of business disciplines features the latest analytics methods of translating data into relevant information for decision-makers. The program emphasizes business data as a valuable asset and shows methods to turn data into actionable insights to enhance operational efficiency, customer value, and profitability. The program uses a hands-on approach with applications in traditional business areas as well as Internet enabled new mediums.

Program outcomes:

  • Rationalize the use of appropriate data sources for a specific operational function and/or research question.
  • Prepare data from public and commercial data sources in order to address specific operational questions.
  • Develop a testable research question that addresses a business/organizational need.
  • Implement domain studies using predictive analytic techniques to enhance decision making for an organization.
  • Formulate business insights found through analytics techniques in a non-technical format online.
  • Integrate business insights found through analytics techniques in a non-technical visual format.
  • Appraise the efficiency of a supply chain for quality improvement.
  • Develop decision-making metrics for supply chain management.

The Master of Science in Computer Science program blends the presentation of theory with hands-on practice. This equips students with a solid foundation of skills, and more importantly, the ability to adapt to the constantly evolving landscape of the computing discipline. The graduates are not only productive in their new jobs, but quickly rise to leadership positions.

A key aspect of this program, as it can prepare students to enter the computer industry directly after graduation, or to continue their educational path to a Philosophy of Doctorate. A variety of electives allow them to customize their experience to suit their interests.

Students are encouraged to explore one of many focus areas currently in demand including: mobile applications, software development, big data, cyber forensics, wireless networking, system administration and more.

An additional feature of the program caters to those wishing to switch fields into the computer science realm. This program has a set of six bridge courses to help students transition from their previous background to a level of readiness that enables them to successfully pursue the rest of the degree program.

The Master of Business Administration program is STEM (science, technology, engineering, and math)-designated by the Department of Homeland Security.

The Data Analytics concentration provides students with a technical awareness of the opportunities needed to enhance business operations. It provides the tools necessary to collect, identify, and understand patterns that allow the organization to make informed decisions consistent with its mission. With a specific focus on the application of mathematical statistics to the description, analysis, and forecasting of business data, the program features the analysis of data from multiple firm sources such as marketing, finance, human resource management, etc. The R-programming language is a central part of the concentration's design.
